Client.title: Client
Client.description: Represents a client of the Warriors Gaming center. The document ID is the Firebase Auth UID.

email.description: Email address of the client, used for authentication.

memberSince.description: The date the client first registered.

subscriptionHours.description: Number of subscription hours remaining for the client.

bonusHours.description: Number of bonus hours accumulated by the client.

usageData.description: Notes on client's usage patterns and preferences.

currentStationId.description: The ID of the station the client is currently using, or null.

Admin.title: Admin
Admin.description: Represents an administrator user. The document ID is the Firebase Auth UID.

Station.title: Station
Station.description: Represents a gaming station (PS5, PC, VIP PS5, VR, Simulator).

type.description: Type of gaming station (PC, PS5, PS5 VIP, VR, Simulator).

status.description: Current status of the station (available, in use, maintenance).

games.description: List of games available on the station.

Reservation.title: Reservation
Reservation.description: Represents a reservation for a gaming station, stored as a subcollection under a client.

clientId.description: Reference to Client UID. (Relationship: Client 1:N Reservation)

UsageLog.title: UsageLog
UsageLog.description: Represents a log of station usage.

clientId.description: Reference to Client UID. (Relationship: Client 1:N UsageLog)

startTime.description: Start time of the station usage.

endTime.description: End time of the station usage.

finalCost.description: The final cost of the session, including any manual adjustments.

ClientHistoryLog.title: ClientHistoryLog
ClientHistoryLog.description: Represents a single event in a client's history.

id.description: Unique identifier for the history log entry.

timestamp.description: The date and time when the event occurred.

description.description: A human-readable description of the event.

id.description: The unique identifier for the setting document.

imageHint.description: A hint for AI image generation tools.

SubscriptionCard.title: Subscription Card
SubscriptionCard.description: Represents a purchasable subscription package that grants hours to a client.

id.description: Unique ID for the subscription card type.

description.description: A short description of what the card offers.

price.description: The cost of the subscription card.

hoursGranted.description: The number of standard subscription hours granted.

bonusHoursGranted.description: The number of bonus hours granted with the purchase.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to manage data for the Warriors Gaming center application, focusing on clients, stations, reservations, and usage logs. The structure emphasizes authorization independence and supports the application's core features, including real-time station monitoring, online reservations, QR code management, and usage analytics.

**Authorization Independence:**
Authorization Independence is achieved by leveraging path-based ownership for private user data (e.g., client profiles) and avoiding hierarchical authorization dependencies (`get()` calls in security rules). There is no explicit collaborative data, so membership maps are not currently required.

**Structural Segregation:**
Data with different access needs is segregated into separate collections. This simplifies security rules by ensuring that all documents within a collection share the same security posture. For instance, client profiles are stored in a dedicated collection (`clients`), separate from station data or reservation information. A subcollection `history` is added under each client to store their activity log, a new `admins` collection is added to store administrator UIDs for role-based access control, and reservations are stored in a subcollection under each client, ensuring data is co-located with the client and can be queried independently and securely.

**Access Modeling:**
- **Client Data:** Each client has their own document in the `clients` collection, accessible to admins for management and to the client themselves (if self-service features are implemented). 
- **Station Data:** Station data is stored in the `stations` collection, and is generally read-only by clients but writable by admins.
- **Reservations and Usage Logs:** Reservations are stored in a subcollection under each client. Usage logs are stored in a separate collection (`usageLogs`). Each document contains references to the relevant client and station, facilitating efficient querying and reporting.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
The structure supports secure `list` operations by ensuring that clients cannot list reservations or usage logs for other clients. Admin can list all clients, stations, reservations, and usage logs.

The structure also supports the integrity of ownership, timestamps, and denormalized data by using atomic operations (transactions/batches) when updating related documents.
